x: Atrocities under s.3(1) carry imprisonment of not less than six months, extendable to five years, and fine.

s: The following act is considered as an atrocity under SC/ST (Prevention of atrocities Act)
o: Dumping waste matter in front of the premises of any member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe
Denial of admission of any member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe in an educational institution
Denial of promotion of any member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe in public employment
Disallowing of any member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe from marrying a forward class member
x:
in 2011 only dumping waste was a listed atrocity among these — now preventing an SC/ST from entering an educational institution is also one (s.3(1)(za)(D), 2015 amendment, in force 26 Jan 2016) (PoA (Amendment) Bill 2014 text, enacted as Act 1 of 2016 (web: prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2014/SC_ST_(Prevention_of_Atrocities)_(A)_bill.pdf))
Dumping excreta, waste matter or carcasses in an SC/ST member's premises or neighbourhood is an atrocity under s.3(1)(ii) of the 1989 Act. (Since the 2015 amendment, preventing entry into an educational institution is also an atrocity.)

s: The provisions for punishment under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act are applicable to which section of people?
o: Only applicable to common citizens but not to government employees to protect them in the function of their duties
To all members (government employees and common people) who are not members of the SC and ST community
To all persons, but only after the primary investigation finds them accused
x: Section 3 applies to 'whoever, not being a member of a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe' – government employees included (public servants get a higher minimum, s.3(2)(vii)).

s: Offence committed by any public servant under Section 3 of the SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, provides for minimum punishment of
x: Section 3(2)(vii): a public servant who commits any offence under s.3 gets not less than one year, extendable to the punishment for that offence.

s: How many Sections are there under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
x: The PoA Act has 23 sections (s.23 = power to make rules); amendments added 14A, 15A and 18A without renumbering.

s: In a prosecution for an offence under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, the accused in his defence cannot take the plea that -
o: The Act was done in exercise of the right of private
He also belongs to the caste as that of the victim
The Act causes such a slight harm which could not be
x:
Printed key: private defence. Strictly the IPC general exceptions, private defence included, still apply to PoA offences, so 'None of the above' is arguable (PoA Act 1989 original text (web: hrw.org/legacy/reports/1999/india/India994-16.h).
The printed key: an atrocity under the PoA Act cannot be defended as the exercise of the right of private defence. The Act also bars anticipatory bail (Sec. 18) and requires the accused to be a non-SC/ST.

s: Under the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, whoever, not being a member of a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe, causes physical harm or mental agony of a member of a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe, on the allegation of practising witchcraft or being a witch shall be punishable
o: with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to five years and with fine.
with imprisonment of a term which shall not be less than six months and with fine.
with imprisonment for a term which shall be one year and with fine.
with imprisonment for term which shall be five years and with fine.
x: The 2015 amendment made causing physical harm or mental agony on the allegation of witchcraft an atrocity (s.3(1)(zb)) – imprisonment not less than six months, extendable to five years, and fine.

s: If a person, not being a member of a SC/ST gives false evidence to convict an SC/ST for a capital offence, the punishment for giving false evidence is
x: Section 3(2)(i): giving or fabricating false evidence to get an SC/ST member convicted of a capital offence – imprisonment for life and fine (death if an innocent is executed).

s: Which of the following Sections of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes Act, 1989 provides for application of certain provisions of the Indian Penal Code?
x: Section 6 applies IPC s.34, Chapters III, IV, V, V-A, s.149 and Chapter XXIII to the Act.

s: In a prosecution for an offence under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, the court can presume which of the following?
x: Section 8: financial assistance to an accused raises a presumption of abetment; a group offence arising from a land or other dispute is presumed to be in furtherance of common intention or common object.

s: As ______ legislation proved to be inadequate, the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act as enacted
x: The PCR Act 1955 and the IPC could not check many forms of atrocities against SCs/STs, so the PoA Act 1989 and Rules 1995 were made.

s: The Preamble of the SC/ST (Prevention of atrocities) Act provides for
o: Recording of evidence of the victims
Providing grants in aid to the victims
x: The long title (preamble) of the 1989 Act: to prevent atrocities, provide Special Courts and provide for the relief and rehabilitation of the victims.

s: Under which Act the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Atrocity Removal Law was implemented?
x: The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act is of 1989 (in force 30 Jan 1990); 1990 is the trap.

s: Which authority has the power to establish a Special Court for speedy trial under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act to provide timely justice to victims?
o: State Government only with the approval of the President
Parliament with the recommendation of the National Commission for SC and ST
State Government alone can do such an arrangement without Central Government approval
With the recommendation of the High Court, the Central Government can do such arrangements
x: Under s.14 the State Government itself specifies a Court of Session as Special Court (with the concurrence of the HC Chief Justice); no Central or Presidential approval is needed. Of the options, 'State Government alone' fits best.

s: Who is empowered for imposition and realization of a collective fine under SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
x: Section 16 PoA Act (power of State Government to impose collective fine) applies s.10A of the PCR Act, so the State Government imposes and realises the fine.

s: An appeal under Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 shall lie from any judgement, sentence or order to the High Court.
x: Section 14A (2015 amendment): an appeal lies from any judgment, sentence or non-interlocutory order of a Special or Exclusive Special Court to the High Court both on facts and on law, within 90 days.

s: Under which Section of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is 'economic boycott' defined ?
x: Section 2(1)(bc), inserted by the 2015 amendment, defines 'economic boycott' (refusal to deal, work for hire or do business etc.).

s: A Court of Session specified as Special Court to try the offences under the Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act for the purpose of providing –
x: Section 14: 'For the purpose of providing for speedy trial' the State Government specifies a Court of Session as a Special Court in each district.

s: Under which of the following Sections of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Act, 1989 is anticipatory bail prohibited?
x: Section 18 PoA Act: s.438 CrPC (anticipatory bail) does not apply to offences under the Act (now BNSS s.482).

s: Who has/had the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
x: Section 23(1): the Central Government may, by notification, make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (PoA Rules 1995).

s: The State Government can specify a Court of Session to be a Special Court to try the offences under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 with the concurrence of the–
x: Section 14: the State Government specifies the Special Court with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court.

s: Which of the following powers is not provided to specified Special Court under Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act?
o: Forfeiture of property of a convict for an offence
To authorize a person for extra investigation other
To remove a person from the area who is suspected
Take measurement and photograph of a person who
x: The Special Court can forfeit property (s.7), remove a likely offender from Scheduled/Tribal areas (s.10) and order measurements and photographs (s.12); conferring police powers on another officer is the State Government's power (s.9), not the court's.

s: Which of the following powers a Special Court cannot exercise under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
o: To take measurement of a person
x: The collective fine is imposed by the State Government (s.16, applying PCR s.10A), not by the Special Court; removal (s.10), forfeiture (s.7) and measurements (s.12) are Special Court powers.

s: Under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, in which section there is a provision for the arrangement of a special court?
x: Section 14 provides for Special Courts (Exclusive Special Courts added in 2015); s.15 Special Public Prosecutors, s.17 preventive action, s.21 duties of Government.

s: In how many days will the investigation officer submit his report for the offences committed under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
x:
Rule 7(2) said 30 days — now investigation and charge-sheet within 60 days (s.4(2)(e) inserted by the 2015 Amendment Act; PoA Amendment Rules, 14 Apr 2016) (PoA (Amendment) Bill 2014 text, enacted as Act 1 of 2016 (web: prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2014/SC_ST_(Prevention_of_Atrocities)_(A)_bill.pdf))
Rule 7(2) of the 1995 Rules required the investigating officer to complete the investigation within 30 days and report to the SP (now 60 days for investigation and charge-sheet, after the 2016 amendments).

s: Investigations over the SC/ST Act has to be carried out by an officer not below the rank of
o: A.C.P. Addition Deputy Commissioner of Police
x: Rule 7(1) of the PoA Rules 1995: an offence under the Act shall be investigated by a police officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police.

s: Under which one of the following Sections of the Scheduled Tribes Rules, 1995 has 'Material for Annual Report' been provided?
x: Rule 18 of the PoA Rules 1995 – 'Material for annual report' (State report to the Centre before 1 July).

s: Under which one of the following Sections of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes Rules, 1995, Constitution of ‘District Level Vigilance and Monitoring Committee’ has been provided?
x: Rule 17 – District-level vigilance and monitoring committee set up by the District Magistrate; Rule 16 is the State-level committee (Chief Minister), Rule 18 the annual report.

s: An offence committed under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 shall be investigated by a police officer, not below the rank of –
x: Rule 7(1) of the PoA Rules 1995: an offence under the Act shall be investigated by a police officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police.

s: The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 broadly covers
x: Minister Thaawarchand Gehlot said the amendments were proposed to broadly cover five areas: offences of atrocities (Chapter II), institutional strengthening, appeals (new s.14A), rights of victims and witnesses (new chapter), and preventive measures.

s: In which of the following cases is it alleged that the verdict of the Supreme Court of India diluted the stringent provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
o: K.C. Vasanth Another vs State of Karnataka
Srish Kumar Choudhury vs State of Tripura
Om Prakash Mahajan vs State of Madhya Pradesh
Subhash Kashinath Mahajan vs State of Maharashtra
x: Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v State of Maharashtra (20 March 2018) was seen as diluting the Act (preliminary enquiry by DSP, anticipatory bail, prior approval); the 2018 amendment (s.18A) reversed it.

s: Which of the following is an Act for protection of rights of socially disadvantaged groups?
o: SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
All the given answers are correct
x: The PCR Act 1955, the PoA Act 1989 and the AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act 1988 all protect socially disadvantaged groups.
